title: 'Venerable Sir, there are over a hundred and fifty training rules that I have to recite every half month. Venerable Sir, I cannot learn them.'…
content: 'Venerable Sir, there are over a hundred and fifty training rules that I have to recite every half month. Venerable Sir, I cannot learn them.' - 'Bhikkhu, can you learn the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training?' - 'Venerable Sir, I can learn the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training.' - 'Therefore, bhikkhu, you should train in the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training. If you train in the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training, then, bhikkhu, through training in these three trainings, greed will be abandoned, hatred will be abandoned, delusion will be abandoned. Through abandoning greed, abandoning hatred, abandoning delusion, you will not do what is unwholesome, you will not follow what is evil.' That bhikkhu, after some time, trained in the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training. Through training in them, greed was abandoned, hatred was abandoned, delusion was abandoned. Through abandoning greed, abandoning hatred, abandoning delusion, he did not do what was unwholesome, he did not follow what was evil.

title: - Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire. And what, Rādha, is suffering? The eye, Rādha, is suffering; therein you should abandon desire.…
content: - Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire. And what, Rādha, is suffering? The eye, Rādha, is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Forms ... Eye-consciousness ... Eye-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact ... that feeling is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. ... The ear ... The nose ... The tongue ... The body ... The mind is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Mind-objects ... Mind-consciousness ... Mind-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact ... that feeling is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire.

title: Elder Vijitasena: I will restrain you like a door restrains an elephant. I will not urge you, O mind, toward evil. You are the net…
content:
Elder Vijitasena:

I will restrain you like a door restrains an elephant.
I will not urge you, O mind, toward evil.
You are the net of sensual desire, you are born from the body.

Restraining you, not going, like an elephant without an open door,
O mind, you sorcerer, though you try again and again,
You will no longer wander, delighting in doing evil.

Like one holding a hook, constantly restraining an untrained elephant,
Like one using force to reform the unwilling —
So toward you, I will reform you.

Like a perfect wheel, like a well-trained horse,
So I will tame you, relying on the five powers.

I will tie you tightly with firm mindfulness.
Having tamed myself, I will tame you.
Through the weight of energy, I will pressure you.
Therefore, O mind, you will not stray from me.

title: Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A…
content:
Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A boil, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A dart, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Bondage, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Mud, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. The womb, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures.
How, bhikkhus, is fear a designation for sensual pleasures? Because those who are infatuated by sensual desire, bound by sensual lust, are not freed from fear in the present life, not freed from fear in the future; therefore, fear is a designation for sensual pleasures.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion;…
content: Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion; one gives out of fear; one gives thinking: 'Earlier our ancestors gave, they did this before. It is not proper for me to let this ancient tradition be neglected'; one gives thinking: 'Having given this gift, after death, with the breakup of the body, I will be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world'; one gives thinking: 'When I give this gift, my mind becomes serene, and joy and happiness arise'; one gives for the adornment of the mind, for the equipment of the mind. Bhikkhus, these are the eight bases for giving.

title: Elder Nun Bhaddā: I am the heir of the Buddha, Kassapa, well-concentrated. I know my past lives, See heavenly and hellish realms. The seer who…
content:
Elder Nun Bhaddā:

I am the heir of the Buddha,
Kassapa, well-concentrated.
I know my past lives,
See heavenly and hellish realms.

The seer who has destroyed birth,
Perfect in direct knowledge,
Along with these three knowledges,
Is a brahmin with three knowledges.

So too, you, Bhaddā Kapilānī,
You are one with three knowledges,
You have destroyed death,
Bearing your final body,
Having conquered Māra's army.

Seeing the danger in the world,
We both went forth.
We are tamed, our taints destroyed,
We are cooled, at peace, liberated.

title: - Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is…
content: - Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is harming me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will harm me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed someone I love, someone I like...' 'He is harming someone I love, someone I like...' 'He will harm someone I love, someone I like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has benefited someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is benefiting someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will benefit someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Getting angry without reason. Bhikkhus, these are the ten grounds for resentment.

title: Bhikkhus, the life span of humans in this world is short, and one must go to the future. Do good deeds, live the holy life.…
content:
Bhikkhus, the life span of humans in this world is short, and one must go to the future. Do good deeds, live the holy life. There is nothing that is born that does not die. Bhikkhus, one who lives long lives only a hundred years, or a little more or less." Then Māra approached the Blessed One and spoke this verse to him:

'Day and night do not pass,
Life span does not end,
The life of humans turns around
Like a chariot wheel around its axle.'

( Blessed One ):
'Day and night do pass,
Life span does end,
The lives of people dry up
Like small streams on a mountain.'

title: - It has been a long time, householder, that you have made this opportunity, namely coming here! - Venerable Sir, for a long time I…
content:
- It has been a long time, householder, that you have made this opportunity, namely coming here!
- Venerable Sir, for a long time I have wanted to see the Blessed One, but I have been busy with these many duties, so I could not come to see the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

One skilled in the Dhamma,
Who has heard much Dhamma,
Does not regard anything
As one's own happiness.

Behold the affliction
Of those who have possessions,
Which causes one person
To be bound to another.

title: - Bhikkhus, it is according to their element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful. The shameful…
content: - Bhikkhus, it is according to their element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful. The shameful associate and come together with the shameful. The fearful associate and come together with the fearful. Those of great learning associate and come together with those of great learning. The energetic associate and come together with the energetic. The mindful associate and come together with the mindful. The wise associate and come together with the wise.
